blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Rank counts only communities with at least ten homes listed. Falling listings with steady sales mean homes are being absorbed faster; rising listings with steady sales mean more choice for buyers. A sellers’ best bet is a community where homes sell quickly against the number listed; a buyers’ best bet is the reverse. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

blocks.text: Between June 2026 and October 2026, detached houses: listings fell from 12 in June to 6 in October (−50.0%), and it took 1.4% of the city’s 141 sales over the period; condos and townhomes: listings rose from 5 in June to 9 in October (+80.0%), and it took 4.3% of the city’s 46 sales over the period.

Mission West here means the western part of the City of Mission, Fraser Valley Regional District, west of Hatzic toward the Stave River: Silverdale, Silverhill, Stave Falls' southern approaches and the Lougheed Highway (Highway 7) corridor west of the town core.
The City's Silverdale Comprehensive Planning Area (SCPA) covers 1,392.16 hectares (3,440.10 acres) in southwest Mission.
Mission's Official Community Plan (OCP) is Bylaw 6405-2026, adopted June 1, 2026, replacing and repealing OCP Bylaw 6350-2025 with the same vision, land use framework, mapping and policy direction.

Existing stock in Mission West proper is rural and suburban single-detached homes on large lots, including Rural 16 Zone (RU16) parcels such as 30748 Silverhill Avenue, at about 1.95 hectares (4.82 acres).

Silverdale is designated for future urban growth, not yet built out: the SCPA Master Infrastructure Strategy (MIS) was done because the area lacks urban servicing (streets, water, sanitary and storm).

blocks.text: Mission West: rules that affect buyers

items.t: Zoning is under City of Mission Zoning Bylaw 5949-2020; a secondary detached unit in RU16 requires rezoning to the secondary-dwelling form, e.g. RU16 to RU16s at 30748 Silverhill Avenue to permit a coach house.
That Silverhill proposal was stated as consistent with the OCP, inside the urban growth boundary, and in the Silverdale Comprehensive Planning Area.

The 2025 OCP referral package was sent to the Agricultural Land Commission (ALC), confirming Agricultural Land Reserve (ALR) land is part of the planning picture in Mission — check the ALC map for a specific lot.

blocks.text: Mission West: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Silverdale's long-range plan splits the SCPA into Central, West and East neighbourhoods; the Central Neighbourhood Plan work includes an Integrated Rainwater Management Plan dated May 31, 2024, prepared for Silverdale Hills GP Inc.

The draft 2025 OCP engagement identified a potential future Transit-Oriented Development Area on Lougheed Highway in Silverdale at the heart of a large Community Node, tied to longer-term servicing expansion.
The Stave River forms Mission's western edge: Hayward Lake and Stave Lake are BC Hydro reservoirs upstream of Ruskin Dam, about 60 km east of Vancouver.
Mission City Station, in town east of this area, is the eastern terminus of the West Coast Express and the meeting point for TransLink and BC Transit buses.

BC Transit Central Fraser Valley routes serving Mission City Station include 31 Valley Connector to Abbotsford, 32 West Heights, 33 Cedar Valley, 34 East Side and 35 Hatzic — no route is named for Silverdale or Steelhead.

blocks.text: Mission West: development and new projects

items.t: Rezoning RSD25-5, 30748 Silverhill Avenue, Silverdale: RU16 to RU16s to permit one secondary detached (coach house) unit on a 1.95 ha lot; information package for the October 6, 2025 meeting.

City of Mission OCP Bylaw 6405-2026, adopted June 1, 2026: replaces and repeals Bylaw 6350-2025 with the vision and framework unchanged. It is the plan framework for Silverdale, the Lougheed corridor and the Rural Mission Strategy.

City of Mission 2026 budget presentation (for a home assessed at $1,133,024 in 2025): flat-rate water user fee $627.24 and sewer user fee $776.64 in the 2026 estimate, refuse collection $164.04 and recycling/compost $292.80 — figures are the City's average-home illustration, not a per-lot quote.
The City's 2026 presentation shows total municipal and utility charges rising 11.74% on that illustration home before relying on it.

West Coast Express: Mission City Station to Waterfront Station, Vancouver, weekday mornings westbound and weekday afternoons eastbound, no weekend or statutory-holiday service; first westbound departure shown 5:25 a.m. in the January 5, 2026 timetable.
TransLink bus 701 provides limited weekday service to and from Mission City Station along Lougheed Highway when trains are not running.

blocks.text: Mission West: risks and due diligence

items.t: Fraser River flood: in June 2026 the Province released new floodplain maps for the Fraser and Coquihalla rivers from Yale to Mission; use the Flood Study Explorer plus the City's own floodplain designation for a specific lot — provincial maps do not replace local designation.
The Province's official Fraser River flood profile runs from Mission to the sea and a separate Hope-to-Mission profile exists; the 1894 flood was the design flood for Fraser dikes.

Silverdale slope and rainwater: the Central Neighbourhood Plan required a dedicated Integrated Rainwater Management Plan and geotechnical assessment, a signal to get lot-level slope and drainage advice in the SCPA hillsides.

faq.q: Can I add a coach house in Silverdale?
faq.a: Not always as-of-right. At 30748 Silverhill Avenue the owner needed a rezoning from RU16 to RU16s (Rural 16 Secondary Dwelling Zone) specifically to permit a secondary detached unit in coach-house form. Ask Planning which secondary-dwelling zone, if any, already applies to the lot you are buying.

faq.q: Is Silverdale serviced for new subdivisions?
faq.a: Not yet at area scale. The City's Master Infrastructure Strategy for the 3,440-acre SCPA exists precisely because the area lacks urban servicing — streets, water, sanitary and storm systems still have to be built as neighbourhood plans proceed. Existing rural homes should be checked lot by lot for well and septic.

School District 75 (Mission). Silverdale Elementary is at 29715 Donatelli Avenue, Mission, and the western side feeds toward Mission's middle and secondary schools in town. Catchments here cover large rural areas, so verify the exact address with the district and ask about bus routing, not just the school name.
The City of Mission's Official Community Plan, Bylaw 6405-2026, adopted June 1, 2026. It also defines the Silverdale Comprehensive Planning Area.
